heroTitle: Reconstruction services after property damage in Southern California
heroIntro: Mitigation stops the damage. Reconstruction puts the home back together. Gallagher Restoration Co. handles the full rebuild phase after water, fire, mold, or sewage events—drywall, insulation, flooring, cabinetry, paint, and fixtures—with insurance-grade documentation and direct coordination with your adjuster across five Southern California counties.

whatItIs.heading: What does reconstruction after property damage involve?
whatItIs.body: Reconstruction is the phase that follows mitigation—the process of rebuilding the areas of a home or commercial property that were damaged, removed during remediation, or destroyed by the original event. After a water loss, reconstruction means replacing the drywall and insulation removed to allow structural drying, relaying flooring, refinishing affected surfaces, and returning the space to its pre-loss condition. After a fire, reconstruction can range from a single room to an entire home: new framing, sheathing, roofing, drywall, insulation, electrical, plumbing, cabinetry, flooring, paint, and trim. Gallagher Restoration Co. operates as a general contractor for the rebuild phase, with in-house crews for core trades and licensed subcontractors for specialized work—plumbing, electrical, HVAC, roofing. The scope is documented in Xactimate-compatible format for insurance, and the same project manager who handled mitigation stays on through the final walkthrough.

steps.title: Scope review and clearance confirmation
steps.body: Before reconstruction begins, Gallagher confirms that mitigation is complete: structural dryness is documented, mold clearance is on file, and any hazardous materials are abated. If another company completed mitigation, a Gallagher technician reviews the drying logs and moisture readings before starting rebuild.

steps.title: Structural rebuild and rough trades
steps.body: Reconstruction begins with framing replacement where structural members were damaged, followed by rough electrical, plumbing, and HVAC work where those systems were affected. Inspections are pulled and passed at each required stage. Insulation, sheathing, and building wrap go in after rough trades are cleared.

steps.title: Drywall, finishes, and interior trades
steps.body: Drywall is hung, taped, and textured to match the existing finish. Flooring—tile, hardwood, LVP, or carpet—is installed after the drywall phase. Cabinetry, trim, paint, and fixtures follow in sequence. The project manager coordinates scheduling so trades do not stack or create rework.

steps.title: Final walkthrough, documentation, and insurance closeout
steps.body: The project closes with a documented final walkthrough reviewing the entire reconstructed area against the original scope. Gallagher delivers a complete project file—before and after photos, permit close-out records, and all trade invoices—formatted for the insurance carrier's final claim settlement.

signs.heading: When you need a reconstruction contractor after property damage
signs.intro: Reconstruction can begin immediately after mitigation clears, or Gallagher can take over after another company has already completed that phase.

items.title: Mitigation is complete and the home needs rebuild
items.body: Once structural drying is documented and any hazardous conditions are cleared, the property is ready for reconstruction. Gallagher can begin scope review and planning the week mitigation closes.

items.title: Another company did mitigation but has no reconstruction capability
items.body: Many mitigation-only companies do not perform reconstruction, leaving homeowners to find a separate contractor mid-claim. Gallagher can review the existing documentation, confirm clearance standards were met, and take over the rebuild phase.

items.title: Insurance has issued a reconstruction estimate and you need a contractor
items.body: An adjuster estimate defines the scope and budget for the rebuild. Gallagher reviews the estimate, identifies any scope gaps, and coordinates with the adjuster before work begins—not after—to avoid disputes at closeout.

items.title: Partial loss: one room or one area of the home
items.body: Not every reconstruction is a whole-home event. A single-room water loss, a kitchen fire limited to cabinets and one wall, or a bathroom requiring full tile and drywall replacement are all jobs Gallagher handles without requiring a full general-contractor buildout.

items.title: Post-fire rebuild where structural and mechanical systems are involved
items.body: Fire reconstruction involving framing, roof structure, electrical panels, or plumbing requires licensed subcontractors and phased inspections. Gallagher coordinates the full trade sequence under one project manager rather than leaving the homeowner to hire and schedule independently.

whyUs.heading: Why homeowners choose Gallagher for post-damage reconstruction
whyUs.body: The gap between mitigation and reconstruction is where most property damage projects fall apart. Two separate companies, two separate schedules, two separate documentation trails, and an insurance adjuster trying to reconcile the difference. Gallagher Restoration Co. closes that gap by operating across both phases—mitigation and reconstruction—under one crew and one project manager. After 15 years of managing full-cycle restoration jobs across Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange, San Diego, and Los Angeles counties, the team understands how insurance documentation works, what inspectors look for at each phase, and how to sequence trades on a tight timeline without rework. Whether the job is a single-room water-damage rebuild in Temecula or a whole-home fire reconstruction in LA County, the same project management discipline applies. Call (951) 541-0034 and a real person answers, around the clock.

pricing.heading: Reconstruction pricing after property damage
pricing.body: Reconstruction costs are driven by the size of the affected area, the trades involved, the materials specified, and the extent of damage to structural systems. A single-room rebuild—drywall, flooring, paint, and trim following a contained water event—typically starts around $5,000. Multi-room reconstruction involving drywall, flooring, cabinetry, and finish work across several areas of a home commonly runs $15,000–$60,000. Whole-home post-fire reconstruction—including framing, mechanical systems, and full finishes—can exceed $150,000 for larger Southern California properties. Gallagher Restoration Co. provides a free on-site assessment to define the scope and produce a written estimate matched to the insurance carrier's documentation requirements. The estimate is the foundation of the claim; starting reconstruction without it in place creates risk of underpayment.

faqs.q: How long does reconstruction take after water or fire damage?
faqs.a: A single-room rebuild following a water loss typically takes one to three weeks once mitigation is complete and materials are on order. Multi-room reconstruction runs four to twelve weeks depending on scope. Full post-fire rebuilds requiring permits, structural work, and mechanical systems can take six to eighteen months, particularly in jurisdictions with permit backlogs. Gallagher builds realistic timelines into the project plan from the start.

faqs.q: Can Gallagher handle reconstruction if a different company did the mitigation?
faqs.a: Yes. Gallagher Restoration Co. can take over the reconstruction phase after any licensed mitigation company has completed and documented their work. A technician reviews the drying logs and clearance documentation before reconstruction begins to confirm mitigation standards were met.

faqs.q: Does my insurance company pay the reconstruction contractor directly?
faqs.a: Payment structures vary by policy and carrier. Some insurers pay the homeowner directly; others issue joint checks. Some release funds in phases tied to project milestones. Gallagher works with homeowners and adjusters to clarify the payment structure before reconstruction begins so there are no surprises at closeout.

faqs.q: What if the insurance estimate does not cover the full reconstruction cost?
faqs.a: Insurance estimates are sometimes incomplete, particularly for older homes where matching existing materials or meeting current code requires upgrades. Gallagher reviews the adjuster's scope, identifies any gaps or code-upgrade requirements, and communicates with the carrier before work begins. Supplement requests supported by documentation have the highest success rate.
